purpose: Acceptance contract for general-language functional 1.0; this document has no live task status and asserts no implementation success.
declared_target: Linux x86_64 native applications and libraries; exact additional supported targets require their own execution evidence.

capabilities.name: Scalars, aggregates and patterns
requirements: All existing scalar widths and checked conversions compose with arrays/slices, Records, Enum, Option and ErrorUnion.
Named and positional patterns preserve nominal identity, visibility, borrowing and actual partial ownership; no silent Copy of exclusive/owning leaves.

capabilities.name: Generic and trait APIs
requirements: Type/const/life arguments, nominal trait/impl identity, associated type/constant projections and ordinary generic/default methods compose across function signatures, fields, aliases and modules.
Unused definitions prove their declared obligations; ambiguity, cycles and illegal overlap are diagnosed before instances can supply missing proofs.
Real iterator/container APIs cover both Copy values and the already supported owning value families.

capabilities.name: Ordinary owned and borrowed data models
requirements: An ordinary Package may own values while retaining external borrows; complete construction, move, nesting, helper return, capture and failure cleanup preserve every actual relation.
Multiple exclusive leaves, reborrow parents and slot initialization/replace/take/refill preserve access and responsibility in the same CFG.
Existing values remain usable together inside ordinary functions; function splitting or a scalar-only seam does not satisfy this capability.

capabilities.name: Heterogeneous runtime abstraction
requirements: Ordinary Unit/value methods and shared/exclusive receivers have real checked dispatch, with provider effects, sources, cleanup and lifetime preserved.
An explicit owned erased-storage route has correct move, destruction and construction-failure behavior for heterogeneous values.

capabilities.name: Stable resource and graph lifecycle
requirements: A runtime-sized graph with cycles/shared edges is constructed, traversed and reclaimed with exact responsibility and no hidden default GC/RC/lease.
Logical deletion and slot reuse cannot revive stale descriptions; static restrictions versus explicit checked operations are documented and exercised.

capabilities.name: Async tasks and cancellation
requirements: Real input ports cover ordinary shared/exclusive values and multiple inputs; PC0, Pending, Ready, cancellation and close preserve actual sources and parent loans.
Typed helper parameters/returns preserve complete retained contexts and move obligations; result borrows distinguish external inputs from the task frame.
Construction failure, PendingExit, notification and cleanup cannot abandon live work or release borrows early.

capabilities.name: Threads, mutex and atomics
requirements: Structured threads, ordinary parameterized Mutex/affine Guard and explicit atomic widths have real machine operations and checked sharing/transfer/cleanup requirements.
Each guard unlocks exactly once, projected borrows depend on the guard, and guard/task/thread transport is permitted only by actual capability proofs.

capabilities.name: Foreign interfaces and registered callbacks
requirements: Native ABI and callback retention have complete unsafe provider contracts and checked lifetime/cleanup behavior.
Callbacks already holding userdata before admission, close races, reentrant close and final drain cannot access reclaimed storage; cross-thread profiles require an actual protocol proof.

capabilities.name: Text, collections, iteration and I/O
requirements: UTF8 validation/encoding, String construction/edit/search/compare and scalar iteration are reusable ordinary APIs.
Dynamic sequences, associative Map/Set, sorting and iterator composition work through actual language-defined APIs, including ordinary owning values and explicit allocation errors.
File/stream I/O distinguishes EOF/error, handles partial writes and cleans actual owned handles on failure and early exit.

capabilities.name: Build, test and dependency workflow
requirements: A documented project manifest, reproducible path dependency resolution/lock, ordinary build/run/check and executable test discovery work from a fresh checkout.
Empty selection, compilation failures, timeouts and failed tests cannot be reported as Pass; diagnostics identify the actual source.

capabilities.name: Supported native delivery
requirements: On the declared Linux x86_64 target, both native backends and O0/O2 execute the same real programs and cleanup/error cases.
Published source is restored independently, all required bytes and dependencies are accounted for, and it builds without prior compiler artifacts.

capabilities.name: Release validation
requirements: Every required capability is bound to actual Source consumers, independent raw/Wire controls where applicable, nonzero executions and precise-source independent review.
No required or unaccounted language profile remains Unsupported; test counts and transport declarations alone are not completion.
Existing validation/product-gates.json remains mandatory for any formal 1.0 product claim; functionality readiness is reported separately from safety/cost/product acceptance.

common_evidence: real ordinary source programs, not simulator-only or isolated IR construction
source commit/tree and actual selected backend/optimization
precise source review by a non-author
construction failure, cleanup and request-budget boundaries when relevant
outside_basic_language_1_0: native Windows support claim without Windows execution
managed execution mode and a default GC/RC
full grapheme/locale typography and advanced IDE services
not_deferred_by_exclusions: ownership/generic/container combinations needed by ordinary libraries
required safety and product acceptance conditions
